summary: The digital transition agenda [now counts 218 structuring projects across six objectives](2026-03-05-governo-aposta-reorganizacao-administracao-publica-governo-digital-2027), up from 214, coordinated by a modernisation institute under the presidency.
developments:
2026-03-05 — the agenda [was restated at 218 structuring projects across six objectives and seven axes, coordinated by a modernisation institute under the presidency](2026-03-05-governo-aposta-reorganizacao-administracao-publica-governo-digital-2027), against 214 when it [was presented abroad in March 2025](2025-03-19-agenda-de-transicao-digital-apresentada-nos-eua).

The project count is the only published progress metric. Nothing states how many of the projects are complete, what any of them cost or which public services they produce, so the agenda's movement over the window is an increase of four in its own inventory.

progress: No change, the absence now documented rather than closed
summary: A readiness assessment [names the absence of an artificial-intelligence strategy as the central gap](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia), with no adoption date, drafting body or timetable on record.
developments:
2026-06-30 — preliminary findings of a UNESCO readiness assessment [were presented to the ministry, identifying the absence of a dedicated artificial-intelligence instrument as the central gap and offering the assessment as the base for future policy](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia).

The same assessment [scores 50.9% of its indicators fully ready, 32.7% partially ready and 16% insufficient, with data governance at 47 out of 100 and science-workforce availability at about 12%](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia). The higher figure quoted elsewhere is the first two bands added together and is not a readiness score.

No adoption date, drafting body or timetable for a strategy is on record. What the country has instead is a draft artificial-intelligence law, reported under legislation, which is an instrument without a policy behind it.

progress: Mixed, a revision consultation closed while an amendment opening electoral data was rejected
summary: The 2011 law [stands unamended](2011-06-17-angola-lei-22-11-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais); [a revision closed consultation](2026-06-17-nova-lei-de-proteccao-de-dados-proximo-ano-legislativo) while [an amendment opening electoral data was rejected](2026-06-25-parlamento-rejeita-proposta-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais).
developments:
The standing instrument [has been in force since 17 June 2011, with consent and notification duties, sensitive-data limits and transfer approvals](2011-06-17-angola-lei-22-11-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais). Three of its provisions matter more than its fines: article 35(6) substitutes a statute or decree for the regulator's authorisation, article 24 does the same for database interconnection, and article 4(2)(a) puts processing under state-secrecy, state-security and judicial-secrecy rules outside the law altogether.

2026-06-17 — public consultation [closed on a revision adding a data-protection officer duty for high-volume processors, stronger oversight and sanction mechanisms, and fines redenominated into local currency](2026-06-17-nova-lei-de-proteccao-de-dados-proximo-ano-legislativo), due at the Council of Ministers and then the National Assembly. No draft text is held.

2026-06-25 — parliament [rejected in plenary an amendment that would have opened the citizen databases and the electoral registers to parties and citizens](2026-06-25-parlamento-rejeita-proposta-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais), after it [had cleared committee in April](2026-04-13-an-aprova-generalidade-alteracao-lei-proteccao-de-dados). The registers stay closed.

summary: The National Assembly [adopted the cybersecurity bill on 12 August 2026 by 104 votes to 56](2026-08-12-angola-cybersecurity-law-approved-angop), with promulgation and entry into force not on file.
developments:
2026-08-12 — the National Assembly [adopted the bill in plenary by 104 votes to 56 on a presidential initiative, the governing party for and the main opposition against with no abstentions](2026-08-12-angola-cybersecurity-law-approved-angop), after [committee approval on 4 August](2026-08-04-angola-proposta-lei-ciberseguranca-especialidade) and [passage in generality in January 2026](2026-01-23-proposta-lei-ciberseguranca-aprovada-generalidade).

The text [sets graduated administrative fines as multiples of the national minimum wage, from 7 to 70 for individuals on minor infractions and up to 500 for individuals and 4,000 for legal persons on the most serious](2026-08-17-angola-loi-cybersecurite-parlement). It also [requires telecommunications operators to transmit any communication whose content is criminal or prejudicial to state security](2026-08-13-angola-cybersecurity-law-approved-pti), which the opposition and part of civil society object to as leaving unclear which content qualifies and on what terms subscribers' personal data reaches the authorities, a year before the presidential election.

No promulgation, gazette number or entry into force is on file. The vote followed a cyberattack on the incumbent operator and came days after the online-falsehoods law entered into force.

summary: The Council of Ministers [approved a civil and criminal identification bill in April 2026](2026-04-29-bi-documento-unico-valido-identificacao), which would set the country's first dedicated identity-data regime.
developments:
2026-04-29 — the Council of Ministers [approved a bill making the identity card the only valid document for banking, telecoms, school enrolment, property registration and contracts, and establishing the country's first dedicated regime for processing identity data](2026-04-29-bi-documento-unico-valido-identificacao). Voter cards, driving licences and passports are currently accepted as substitutes.

No parliamentary stage has been recorded since. Two other instruments touch the same ground and neither is this one: [an electoral registration law replacing in-person enrolment with automatic enrolment from the civil identity database](2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report), which reaches the base only through a secondary account with no gazette reference, and the data protection law reported above, which is the general regime the identity-specific one would sit beside.

summary: An 86-article artificial-intelligence bill [went to public consultation in September 2025](2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial), with no tabling, committee stage or vote since.
developments:
The draft [runs to 86 articles in nine chapters](2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial) and departs from the tiered risk pyramid used elsewhere: [a single critical-AI category carries registration, security-risk assessment and emergency-response duties, with extraterritorial reach over activity abroad affecting Angolan interests, a right to explanation and to refuse decisions made by artificial intelligence, and both criminal and strict civil liability](2025-12-29 Review of Angola's Proposed Law on Artificial Intelligence).

It repeals no existing legislation, defers military applications to a separate instrument and excludes scientific research and purely personal use. Its financial assessment is not costed.

No tabling, committee stage or vote is on record in the eleven months since consultation opened, and the policy the law would implement does not exist: the readiness assessment reported under strategy names its absence as the central gap.

summary: The authority [published a third fine in August 2026](2026-08-19-sapo-angola-apd-fine-hotel-diamante), reaching commercial controllers outside the technology sector, with [three of seven board seats filled](2026-06-26-apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-crescer-tech-fast-digital-center).
developments:
Enforcement is the movement. 2026-06-26 — [millionaire fines were applied to two technology firms](2026-06-26-apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-crescer-tech-fast-digital-center), and 2026-08-19 — [a US$115,000 penalty followed against a hotel](2026-08-19-sapo-angola-apd-fine-hotel-diamante), which is the first published sanction against an ordinary commercial controller outside the technology sector. These follow [a 2024 wave that included the incumbent telecoms operator](2024-08-10 Angola - Dados Pessoais e Ciber-seguranca (APD enforcement)). Deliberation texts and dates are not published and the newest penalty is reported in dollars rather than kwanza, so no running total can be stated in one currency.

Its constitution is the standing weakness. [Three of the seven board seats are filled](2019-09-06-angola-decreto-presidencial-277-19-nomeacao-conselho-administracao-apd) and the four the National Assembly and the judiciary elect are not established as ever having been filled; every member [is removable by presidential decree at any time and without stated grounds](2016-10-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-214-16-estatuto-organico-apd); and the body [retains 60% of the fines and fees it levies](2021-03-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-60-21-regulamento-taxas-apd), revenue onto which [a pay decree moved most of each board member's salary from May 2024](2021-05-25-angola-decreto-presidencial-126-21-estatuto-remuneratorio-apd).

progress: No change, the gaps newly documented rather than closed
summary: State surveillance [runs without judicial warrant at any stage](2020-04-23-angola-lei-11-20-vigilancia-electronica), and [no rule states when the intelligence service may obtain identity, biometric or mobility data](2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report).
developments:
The surveillance regime [has been in force since April 2020: cellular location and electronic surveillance are authorised in writing by the public prosecutor, or by the head of the police body in urgent cases with notice within 72 hours, with no judicial warrant at any stage and execution running 90 days renewable](2020-04-23-angola-lei-11-20-vigilancia-electronica). Private persons and businesses must open their own video-surveillance systems to the criminal police, and the data-protection authority is given knowledge and monitoring of the resulting police database rather than authorisation over it.

Alongside it, [video-surveillance installations are licensed by the minister responsible for public security and recordings are erased at 30 days unless a criminal-police or judicial body has requested them](2021-12-21-angola-decreto-presidencial-308-21-regulamento-videovigilancia).

2026-08-15 — a civil-society report [documents what is missing: no rule for intelligence access to identity, biometric or mobility data, no independent review of such requests, and a border-control system budgeted at US$112m and awarded directly, where the one functional post has discontinued fingerprint capture](2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report). The only evidence of use on file is [a forensic confirmation that an intelligence service acquired commercial spyware and infected a journalist's phone](2026-02-26-sinse-adquiriu-spyware-predator-para-espiar-jornalista).

summary: A neighbouring state operator [began proof-of-concept testing on the Angolan satellite](2026-08-25-tmcel-angosat2-satellite-trials-itweb), a first step toward selling national space capacity across the region.
developments:
2026-08-25 — Mozambique's state operator [began proof-of-concept testing of the Angolan satellite for telecommunications services in Mozambique, announced by the Angolan telecommunications ministry as a step towards a commercial agreement to distribute communication and broadcasting signals over Angolan space infrastructure](2026-08-25-tmcel-angosat2-satellite-trials-itweb).

It follows the Mozambican public broadcaster's own proof of concept transmitting its television signal via the satellite, implements a bilateral memorandum signed in June 2026, and runs in parallel with a commercial pilot agreement with a Namibian operator for satellite-driven backhaul. Both trials are framed as advancing the ICT priority of the regional infrastructure master plan.

No commercial terms are published, and neither trial has yet become a contract. This is the only case on the ledger of the country exporting digital infrastructure rather than importing it.

summary: A false-information law [entered into force on 4 August 2026](2026-08-06-angola-lei-informacoes-falsas-diario-republica) carrying prison terms, and [journalists' bodies warn it will inhibit citizen journalism](2026-08-22-novojornal-jornalistas-advertem-lei-inibir-jornalismo-cidadania).
developments:
2026-08-06 — the law [was gazetted as Lei n. 6/26 and entered into force on 4 August 2026, after the National Assembly passed it 105 to 72 in May with only the main opposition against](2026-08-06-angola-lei-informacoes-falsas-diario-republica). It [carries fines of 200 to 400 minimum wages, one to three years for simple publication, three to eight where it incites hatred or damages reputation, and up to ten in the aggravated case](2026-08-06-angola-fake-news-law-enters-force), and [binds telecommunications operators, digital platforms and application providers, reaches content aimed at the domestic public from outside the country, and bans inauthentic accounts](2026-08-17-plmj-angola-lei-6-26-fake-news).

2026-08-22 — the journalists' union, the professional credential and ethics commission and the women journalists' forum [warned that the law will inhibit citizen journalism, arguing that its penalties are excessive and that whether something counts as a journalistic error will depend heavily on how the courts and the aggrieved party read it](2026-08-22-novojornal-jornalistas-advertem-lei-inibir-jornalismo-cidadania).

No enforcement action anywhere in the country is held, and [civil society had raised the same objections as it came into force](2026-08-10-angola-false-information-law-in-force-civil-society). The account of the text held is a law-firm note rather than the gazetted instrument.

summary: The communications programme [was cut 30.5% for 2026](2026-02-20-ago-oge-2026-comunicacoes-programa-corte) and cybersecurity [by 54%](2025-11-06-ago-oge-2026-ciberseguranca-32bn), while [US$275m](2026-02-26-credito-suplementar-275-milhoes-usd-mat-bdcm) and [US$218.5m](2025-09-19-ago-dp-169-25-bilhete-identidade-credito-adicional) supplementary credits opened.
developments:
The president authorised US$210.91m for an integrated ecosystem of state digital services ([authorisation](2026-08-31-ago-governo-210-milhoes-digitalizacao-administracao)), with US$13m for the public administration interoperability platform ([authorisation](2026-08-31-ago-pti-interoperabilidade-13-milhoes)) and US$4.6m to strengthen state cybersecurity ([authorisation](2026-08-31-ago-diariodosnegocios-ciberseguranca-4-6-milhoes)). These are authorisations to spend, not disbursements.

The recurrent lines fell. [Kz 159.2bn was appropriated to the communications programme for 2026 against Kz 229.3bn for 2025, a cut of 30.5%, with fourth-generation expansion down 42% to Kz 62.7bn and the third-generation coverage line deleted](2026-02-20-ago-oge-2026-comunicacoes-programa-corte). [The cyber-security line fell from Kz 70.5bn to Kz 32.3bn, about 54%](2025-11-06-ago-oge-2026-ciberseguranca-32bn), read at draft stage before enactment.

The identity programme was financed outside the budget cycle instead. [US$218,500,000 of supplementary credit was gazetted to the justice ministry for identity-card universalisation](2025-09-19-ago-dp-169-25-bilhete-identidade-credito-adicional), and [US$275,000,000 was opened inside the 2026 budget for the adult-citizen database proof-of-life update, more than doubling the territorial administration ministry's allocation](2026-02-26-credito-suplementar-275-milhoes-usd-mat-bdcm).

Execution is the weak point. The first per-organ table published [shows 3% first-quarter execution, with 20 of 50 programmes below 5%](2026-04-29-ago-oge-2026-i-trimestre-execucao-lei-identificacao). No released, actual or audited figure is held for either budget year.

summary: The data-protection authority [signed a mutual-assistance memorandum with a Lusophone counterpart in September 2025](2025-09-18-nadpa-angola-brazil-dpa-mou), its first bilateral with a non-African regulator.
developments:
2025-09-18 — at a global privacy assembly, the authority [signed a bilateral memorandum providing mutual assistance and technical, regulatory and supervisory cooperation](2025-09-18-nadpa-angola-brazil-dpa-mou). No bilateral with any non-African regulator was held before it.

A stated intention to conclude a similar arrangement elsewhere is unevidenced, and no activity under the memorandum has been reported since signature. It is the only regulator-to-regulator instrument on this ledger; every other agreement recorded for the country is with a vendor, a lender or a foreign government, and those are reported under geopolitics.

summary: The incumbent operator's [15% stake sale raised about US$329m at 120.72% subscription](2026-07-28-angola-unitel-15-percent-stake-sale), alongside [a fintech investment](2026-06-26-proparco-supports-anda-angola) and [a private-credit fund](2026-03-30-bfa-asset-management-kimbo-fund-angola-startups).
developments:
2026-07-28 — [15% of the incumbent operator's capital and votes were sold for Kz 300.3bn, reported as about US$329m, at 120.72% subscription, creating 11,264 new shareholders](2026-07-28-angola-unitel-15-percent-stake-sale), after [the offering opened earlier in July](2026-07-07-unitel-opens-angola-share-offering). One consequence is regulatory: disclosure of the July cyberattack now runs under securities law rather than telecoms regulation.

2026-06-26 — a development finance institution [invested in a mobility fintech](2026-06-26-proparco-supports-anda-angola), [with no amount, instrument, tenor or stake disclosed](2026-06-26-proparco-invests-in-angolas-anda).

2026-03-30 — [the country's first private-credit vehicle for small and mid-market firms made a second deployment, anchored by a US$5m sovereign-fund commitment in 2024](2026-03-30-bfa-asset-management-kimbo-fund-angola-startups), with no fund size or investor list beyond the anchor published.

summary: The digital acceleration loan [reached US$112.21m disbursed of US$300m with both ratings lifted](2026-06-10-world-bank-angola-digital-acceleration-isr-seq4), while [every outcome indicator still reads zero](2026-07-31-pada-projecto-aceleracao-digital-abrange-10-milhoes-de-pessoas).
developments:
2026-06-10 — [US$112.21m of the US$300m was disbursed at 10 June 2026, 37.40%, with both World Bank ratings lifted to Moderately Satisfactory](2026-06-10-world-bank-angola-digital-acceleration-isr-seq4), from [ratings cut to Moderately Unsatisfactory in April 2025 with nothing disbursed](2025-04-11-world-bank-angola-digital-acceleration-isr-2025-04). [The loan was signed on 11 October 2024 on non-concessional terms carrying a front-end fee and a variable spread](2024-10-11-worldbank-loan-agreement-9693-ao-angola-digital-acceleration).

Money moved and results did not. [Every project outcome indicator read zero as at 30 April 2026 against March 2030 targets of 13,500,000 people using broadband internet, 10,000,000 with digitally verifiable identification, 100,000 trained through digital literacy programmes and 400 firms adopting digital technologies](2026-07-31-pada-projecto-aceleracao-digital-abrange-10-milhoes-de-pessoas).

Three other partners are on the ledger: [a US$250m civil registration and local governance project rehabilitating birth-registration posts](2026-04-06-projecto-njila-reabilita-postos-de-registo-bie-huambo), [a US$60m statistical capacity loan running to 2027](2022-03-25-wb-ago-002-angola-strengthening-statistical-capacity) with no disbursement or results figure on file, and [US$87m of Korean export-credit financing for five municipal command and control centres, phase two of which broke ground in February 2026](2026-02-12-pn-reforca-seguranca-cinco-novos-centros-comando-controlo) with no data-protection basis, retention rule or supervisory authority named for the camera estate.

progress: Advanced, on network build, with no subscriber series on the base
summary: A third operator [installed 20 towers in an exclave province](2026-08-19-angop-africell-cabinda) and [enterprise 5G launched commercially](2026-07-23-angola-mercury-my5g-cabinda-launch); no national subscriber figure is published.
developments:
2026-08-19 — the third network [installed 20 telecommunications towers in the exclave province of Cabinda with satellite backhaul agreed, stating commercial voice, data and satellite-linked service would start within days](2026-08-19-angop-africell-cabinda). No coverage percentage, investment figure, population reached or launch date is published, and "in the coming days" is the whole of the commitment held.

2026-07-23 — [an enterprise 5G service launched commercially in the same province, with the capital at over 70% city coverage, about US$20m budgeted and every provincial capital targeted by 2027](2026-07-23-angola-mercury-my5g-cabinda-launch). This is enterprise connectivity rather than consumer mobile, and the throughput figures are the operator's own.

2026-06-11 — [national roaming and infrastructure sharing extended voice and data to remote areas through shared towers, solar power and satellite backhaul](2026-06-11-ilumina-angola-conectividade-no-lago-dilolo), with no national site count, budget or target published. The standalone fifth-generation network [remains at a trial call in a live environment with no commercial launch date](2025-03-06-unitel-ericsson-angola-network-modernization), on a vendor release.

No regulator return and no operator subscriber total appears anywhere on this ledger, so penetration itself is unmeasured.

summary: Five official statements of fibre length [run non-monotonic between 20,000 km and 30,000 km](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia), and the base asserts no current national figure.
developments:
The measurement is the finding. Official statements put the terrestrial network at [22,000 km in 2023](2023-05-17-minttics-matias-borges-22000km-rede-fibra-optica-terrestre), 20,000 in October 2025, [30,000 in November 2025](2025-11-28-angola-30000km-terrestrial-fibre-itu-wtdc-baku), 22,000 in April 2026 and [28,000 in June 2026](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia). The series is not monotonic and no definition accompanies any of the figures, so the base asserts no current national length. The regulator's annual statistical report that would settle it was dropped as unobtainable.

The build behind the figures is equally opaque. [The national broadband network was financed by a specific loan agreement of about US$249m signed in October 2023](2023-01-01-eximbank-cn-ago-003-national-broadband-infrastructure-upgrading-project-rnbl) and remains active with no delivery milestone published at either end. [A domestic submarine cable to interlink the coastal cities and connect a transport corridor to an international system was stated as in preparation in March 2026](2026-03-26-minttics-projectos-estruturantes-base-tecnologica), with no route, cost, financier or date.

summary: A new cable branch [entered service with 23.6 Tbps allocated to Angola](2025-12-13-unitel-investe-43-milhoes-usd-ramal-2africa), and [1.0 Tbps was contracted through a neighbouring landing](2026-06-15-telecom-namibia-angola-telecom-satcab-sarssy-1tbps).
developments:
2025-12-13 — the 2Africa branch and its landing station [were inaugurated and switched on, built by the incumbent for US$43m, with 23.6 Tbps of the cable's capacity allocated to Angola, replacing an end-of-life system and one already at capacity](2025-12-13-unitel-investe-43-milhoes-usd-ramal-2africa). The incumbent is the only Angolan member of the consortium.

2026-06-15 — the state operator [signed a master service agreement for an initial 1.0 Tbps of dedicated capacity through a Namibian landing of the Equiano cable, with an option to assume ownership](2026-06-15-telecom-namibia-angola-telecom-satcab-sarssy-1tbps); design, testing, commissioning and handover are still to run, and the country reaches that cable only indirectly.

[Further submarine expansion is stated as ministry policy](2025-11-07-minttics-expandir-rede-de-fibra-optica-submarina). No price, utilisation or wholesale capacity figure is published for any of it, so the base can state what has been added and not what it costs or carries.

progress: Advanced, one operator now commercially deployed while another application stands unresolved
summary: A low-orbit licence [reached a multi-year capacity agreement](2026-06-12-mercury-eutelsat-acordo-conectividade-leo) and [a first reseller was licensed on the national satellite](2026-07-02-startup-do-moxico-licenca-internet-via-angosat-2), while [one application is unresolved](2026-08-03-starlink-em-angola-conectividade-controlo-e-a-politica-silenciosa-do-ceu).
developments:
2026-06-12 — the country's [first and only licensed low-orbit operator, granted a 15-year licence in June 2025 with a Luanda ground station](2025-06-30-eutelsat-secures-15-year-oneweb-licence-in-angola), [moved from licence to commercial deployment through a multi-year capacity agreement with a local provider](2026-06-12-mercury-eutelsat-acordo-conectividade-leo).

2026-07-02 — on the national satellite, [a commercial access hub opened in December 2025 with 37 firms in the integration process by April 2026, and a first startup was licensed to resell access](2026-07-02-startup-do-moxico-licenca-internet-via-angosat-2). Bandwidth, pricing and operator access terms remain undisclosed.

2026-08-03 — the largest low-orbit operator [is still unlicensed, with a secretary of state saying only that the process is under way and the regulator still working out how to fit low-orbit operators into a regime written for terrestrial networks](2026-08-03-starlink-em-angola-conectividade-controlo-e-a-politica-silenciosa-do-ceu). Sixteen months of identical status is the finding, the position being unchanged since [the ministry said negotiations were continuing in April 2025](2025-04-16-angola-minttics-negociacoes-starlink-continuam).

progress: Mixed, a Tier III commercial facility in service while the only Tier IV project has been silent for three years
summary: A commercial data centre [opened at up to 3 MW over more than 800 racks](2025-10-02 Raxio Opens Angola's Largest Data Centre in Landmark 30 Million Expansion), while [the only Tier IV project](2023-06-27 Paratus to build third Angola data center (DC3, Tier IV)) has produced nothing since 2023.
developments:
2025-10-02 — the country's first Tier III commercial facility [opened at up to 3 MW and more than 800 racks over 19,000 square metres on US$30m, near the cable landings, with a plan to exceed 7 MW within five years](2025-10-02 Raxio Opens Angola's Largest Data Centre in Landmark 30 Million Expansion). Its operator [contracted six times as much power across its group in the first half of 2026 as a year earlier](2026-07-23-raxio-afr-ix-data-centres-angola-mozambique).

Against it, [a second commercial project announced in 2023 as the country's first Tier IV facility at over 10 MW and 2,000 racks, financed but not built](2023-06-27 Paratus to build third Angola data center (DC3, Tier IV)), has no source since and never had a stated completion date. Three years of silence on the only Tier IV project in the country is the counterweight to one facility opening.

summary: The government data centre [was inaugurated in April 2026 at 208 racks and 1,040 kW](2026-04-28-pr-inaugura-novo-centro-de-dados-do-governo), carrying [a national cloud under a mandatory migration](2026-04-28-centro-de-dados-do-governo-soberania-digital).
developments:
2026-04-28 — the President [inaugurated the government data centre: 6,225 square metres, Tier III design, 208 racks and 1,040 kW live in a modular design of about 336-rack capacity, reported at about US$89m](2026-04-28-pr-inaugura-novo-centro-de-dados-do-governo), from [about 75% complete in November 2025](2025-11-14 Angola Nears Completion of National Data Center, Set for 2026 Launch), with a second account giving about US$90m and no kwanza original published.

The same day, [a unified government cloud entered operation under a progressive and mandatory migration of public services, framed as repatriating passports and education certificates from foreign platforms](2026-04-28-centro-de-dados-do-governo-soberania-digital), against [a first stone laid in September 2025 with a migration mandate stated and nothing yet to migrate onto](2025-09-10 Angola advances technological development for digital transformation).

No source records how much has actually migrated, so the capacity is established and its use is not.

2026-09-02 — a commercial operator disclosed a data centre installed at Lobito as the technical support and data-management platform behind its coastal internet and television services ([inauguration](2026-09-02-zap-fibra-benguela-angola)). No capacity, rack count or power figure accompanies it, which is the same silence the fibre-length series shows: facilities are announced and none of them is measured.

progress: No change, a first record of an export commitment with no domestic load figure behind it
summary: A [US$1.5bn, 1,200MW line to carry surplus Angolan hydropower to the DRC](2025-10-16-mitrelli-hydro-link-angola-drc-power-line) was agreed in October 2025; no domestic data-centre load figure is held.
developments:
2025-10-14 - a New York-based energy investor and the DRC government [signed a memorandum of understanding for a 1,150 km, US$1.5bn, 1,200MW transmission line carrying surplus Angolan hydropower to the DRC, targeted for completion in 2029 and aimed principally at the Copperbelt mining sector](2025-10-16-mitrelli-hydro-link-angola-drc-power-line).

Angola is the source of the power and not a party to the memorandum on the record, and no Angolan offtake, tariff or financing close is published. Nor does the base hold any figure for data-centre load, generation headroom or water use in Angola, so what a 1,200MW export commitment leaves for domestic digital infrastructure cannot be stated here.

progress: Mixed, household access rose across the census cycle while the electrification target year passed with no outturn published
summary: Household access [reached 48.6% at the 2024 census, 8.5% rural](2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos), while [the 60% target for 2025](2023-07-04 AD664 - Lack of grid access plagues most rural residents in Angola) passed unmeasured.
developments:
2025-11-20 — definitive census results [put household access to electricity at 48.6% at the 2024 reference date, 68.9% urban against 8.5% rural, from 31.9% at the 2014 census](2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos). That is the physical floor under every system named in this report.

Against it, [a Power Sector Action Plan target of 60% electrification by 2025, from 47% in 2020](2023-07-04 AD664 - Lack of grid access plagues most rural residents in Angola), reached its target year with no electrification rate published since the 2020 baseline. The census figure is a different measure on a different definition and cannot be read as the outturn.

The rural figure is the one that matters for the connectivity and registration programmes reported elsewhere: at that level, mains power is not an assumption a rural service can be designed on.

summary: The statistics office [built its census portal and mobile application with its own staff](2026-07-02-ine-lanca-portal-do-censo-2024-e-aplicacao-movel), and the tax authority [states it builds and feeds its risk-analysis system in-house](2026-02-11-inteligencia-artificial-coloca-incumpridores-sob-analise-reforcada-da-agt).
developments:
Two agencies report building their own systems. 2026-07-02 — [a public census portal carrying demographic, social, economic and housing indicators by geographic level, plus a mobile application with macroeconomic series, was built by the statistics office's own staff](2026-07-02-ine-lanca-portal-do-censo-2024-e-aplicacao-movel). 2026-02-11 — [the tax authority states that it builds and feeds its machine-learning risk-analysis system in-house](2026-02-11-inteligencia-artificial-coloca-incumpridores-sob-analise-reforcada-da-agt), with no model, supplier or accuracy figure published.

Everything else of scale is contracted out, and the two largest identity and interoperability procurements of the window are reported under data exchange and digital identity. Nothing on the ledger states a headcount, a skills audit or a retention position for government technical staff, so the two in-house builds are the whole of the evidence either way.

progress: Mixed, a strategy, a council and a centre created on paper while the budget was cut and a national outage ran nine days
summary: A strategy, a council and a cyber centre [were created by decree](2025-12-03-decreto-presidencial-256-25-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-angola), none with an operating record, while [an attack took the incumbent's services down for nine days](2026-08-06-angola-unitel-completes-restoration-of-mobile-services).
developments:
The instruments arrived together. [A national cybersecurity strategy was gazetted on 3 December 2025 with six strategic objectives and a two-phase legislative reform](2025-12-03-decreto-presidencial-256-25-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-angola), [a consultative national cybersecurity council chaired by the President was created by decree the same day](2025-12-03-decreto-presidencial-258-25-conselho-nacional-ciberseguranca-angola), and [a national cybersecurity centre was constituted as a public institute with regulatory, supervisory, inspection and sanctioning powers, an emergency response team and a round-the-clock operations department, retaining 30% of the fines it levies](2025-12-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-263-25-centro-nacional-ciberseguranca). None has an operating record: no source records the council convening or the centre exercising any power, and [in August 2026 the responsible minister was still describing the centre's launch in the future tense](2026-08-10-angola-national-cybersecurity-centre-telecompaper). The cybersecurity fund its statute presupposes is created by no instrument on file.

The operational test went badly. [An attack on the incumbent from the early hours of 28 July 2026 took voice, messaging, mobile data and internet down nationwide until 5 August, nine days](2026-08-06-angola-unitel-completes-restoration-of-mobile-services), with [full restoration declared on 21 August bar one feature](2026-08-21-tan-unitel-angola-restores-services-cyberattack) and [automatic compensation to customers](2026-08-20-angop-unitel-compensa-clientes-pelo-ataque-cibernetico). Every account is the operator's own; no regulator finding, attacker, vector or outage cost is published.

[Analysts argued afterwards that telecommunications should be designated critical infrastructure](2026-07-29-angola-unitel-attack-critical-digital-infrastructure-experts); no designation instrument exists.

summary: A [US$150m contract for the interoperability platform, digital signatures and digital identity entered execution on 31 July 2026](2026-08-04-angola-ima-launches-public-digital-infrastructure-project-with-tis), by sole-referenced award.
developments:
2026-08-04 — [a US$150m twelve-month contract entered execution on 31 July 2026 for a secure-zone critical-computing component hosting the interoperability platform, key-based electronic signatures, digital identity and structured cybersecurity, financed under a presidential order and inscribed in the 2026 public investment programme](2026-08-04-angola-ima-launches-public-digital-infrastructure-project-with-tis). [The contract itself was signed in June 2026](2026-06-17-ima-tis-contrato-projecto-infra-estruturas-digitais-publicas) and [carried in the year's investment programme](2026-06-17-ago-2026-ima-infra-estruturas-digitais-publicas).

It is a sole-referenced state technology award under a presidential order, with the procurement route unstated. No national interoperability platform was in service before it, and no technical standard, published interface or exchange volume is on file — so the country has a contract for an exchange layer and not yet the layer.

summary: A tender [opened for a US$28m national digital identity and electronic signature platform](2026-08-14-angola-digital-identity-platform-usd28m-pti), separate from the card, which [is now generated from the birth record](2026-07-01-impressao-do-bi-abrange-todas-as-provincias).
developments:
2026-08-14 — the President [authorised US$28m and formally opened a public tender for a National Digital Identity and Electronic Signatures Platform, specified to support up to 30 million digital identities and to let citizens, firms and public officials use a single digital credential for public services, digital contracts, electronic verification of customers and legally valid electronic signatures](2026-08-14-angola-digital-identity-platform-usd28m-pti). It [was named as a workstream in the 2024 loan agreement with nothing built](2024-10-11-worldbank-loan-agreement-9693-ao-angola-digital-acceleration). No supplier, timetable or relationship to the separately recorded public digital infrastructure contract is stated.

The physical credential is distinct and unchanged: [in issue nationwide and generated from the birth record by system interoperability](2026-07-01-impressao-do-bi-abrange-todas-as-provincias), on [a foreign-built platform running since 2017](2017-01-16-nj-chineses-apoiam-angola-emissao-bi-registo-nascimento). What moved on it is its measurement and its proposed legal monopoly, both reported elsewhere in this report.

progress: Advanced, on issuance capacity, with coverage measured for the first time rather than raised
summary: The census [put card coverage at 52.4% of those aged five and over, leaving 14.9m undocumented](2025-11-26-quase-metade-dos-angolanos-sem-bilhete-de-identidade), against [a universalisation plan now printing in all 21 provinces](2026-08-18-minjusdh-programa-universalizacao-bi-egito-praia).
developments:
2025-11-26 — the first national coverage figure the base holds [puts 52.4% of the population aged five and over as holding the card, 63% urban against 30.9% rural, leaving 14.9m people undocumented](2025-11-26-quase-metade-dos-angolanos-sem-bilhete-de-identidade), drawn from [the 2024 census definitive results](2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos). Before it, a 2023 diagnostic said only that the country was far from universal coverage. The movement is in measurement rather than in coverage.

Issuance capacity did move. [A universalisation programme runs printing posts in all 21 provincial capitals with two to three printers per province planned, mobile brigades in remote municipalities and three phases covering unregistered adults, cards at birth and replacement of degraded documents; one provincial campaign issued and delivered more than 4,000 cards in 16 days in a single municipality](2026-08-18-minjusdh-programa-universalizacao-bi-egito-praia), and [the ministry has been opening identification posts through the year](2026-08-01-angola-ministro-justica-postos-identificacao).

Collection is the leak. [More than 120,000 issued cards were awaiting collection at identification posts nationwide in July 2026](2026-07-15-mais-de-120-mil-bilhetes-aguardam-levantamento), the first such figure held and with no prior series to read it against.

progress: Advanced, on printing capacity, with the platform itself foreign-built
summary: Card printing [moved from a single national centre to all 21 provinces from 1 July 2026](2026-07-01-impressao-do-bi-abrange-todas-as-provincias), on [a platform built abroad since 2017](2017-01-16-nj-chineses-apoiam-angola-emissao-bi-registo-nascimento).
developments:
2026-07-01 — [all 21 provinces began printing the identity card locally, with two to three printers per province planned and a 24-to-48-hour issuance target; one province reports issuance under 24 hours against one to two weeks before](2026-07-01-impressao-do-bi-abrange-todas-as-provincias), and [the same decentralisation reached the exclave province in July](2026-07-28-angola-cabinda-decentralised-id-card-service). This is printing only: enrolment and biometric capture are untouched.

Underneath it, [the card has been issued on a foreign-built platform since 2017](2017-01-16-nj-chineses-apoiam-angola-emissao-bi-registo-nascimento), and the digital identity platform now out to tender is also to be procured rather than built. No source states who maintains either system, what the support arrangements are, or whether source code or operational control sits with the State — which is the question this indicator asks and the record does not answer.

summary: Parliament [granted legislative authorisation for an electronic signature and certification regime](2026-07-30-angola-parliament-electronic-signature-legislative-authorisation), and [a public key infrastructure was contracted](2026-06-17-ima-tis-contrato-projecto-infra-estruturas-digitais-publicas) ahead of it.
developments:
2026-07-30 — parliament [unanimously approved legislative authorisation to the President, valid 90 days after publication of the enabling law, for a regime defining an accrediting authority, a root certification entity and the evidential weight of an electronic signature](2026-07-30-angola-parliament-electronic-signature-legislative-authorisation), grounded on the insufficiency of two 2011 instruments. The substantive text will be an executive instrument and is not yet made.

The technology is ahead of the law. [A public key and time-stamp infrastructure was announced as a ministerial intention in June 2025 with nothing contracted and no legal basis](2025-06-30-infra-estrutura-de-chaves-publicas-e-carimbo-do-tempo); it [is now contracted as a component of the US$150m public digital infrastructure project](2026-06-17-ima-tis-contrato-projecto-infra-estruturas-digitais-publicas), and [the tax authority is already running mandatory electronic invoicing on it in practice](2026-05-23-agt-eliminacao-gradual-documentos-em-papel). The trust layer is being built ahead of the law that would govern it.

summary: Registry posts [opened in maternity wards in one province so newborns leave registered and issued a first identity card](2026-03-04-zaire-inicia-registo-de-recem-nascidos-na-maternidade), with no national rollout published.
developments:
2026-03-04 — [registry posts in maternity wards were launched in one province, running there since October 2025, so that newborns leave registered and issued a first identity card, foreign-funded with United Nations support](2026-03-04-zaire-inicia-registo-de-recem-nascidos-na-maternidade), following [the start of card issuance to newborns in November 2025](2025-11-17 Angola begins issuance of ID cards to newborns).

No national rollout map, no registration count and no target is published, so what the base holds is one province and a stated model. The universalisation programme reported under registration names cards at birth as one of its three phases, which is the nearest thing to a plan on file.

The measure that would test it runs the other way: birth registration among children aged nought to four is the weakest cohort in the census, reported under the civil register.

summary: The identity card [is generated from the birth record by system interoperability](2026-07-01-impressao-do-bi-abrange-todas-as-provincias), a link [standing since 2017](2017-01-16-nj-chineses-apoiam-angola-emissao-bi-registo-nascimento) and unmeasured since.
developments:
The link exists and is old. [The card is generated from the birth record by system interoperability](2026-07-01-impressao-do-bi-abrange-todas-as-provincias), on [a platform installed with foreign assistance in 2017 that tied card issuance to birth registration from the start](2017-01-16-nj-chineses-apoiam-angola-emissao-bi-registo-nascimento).

Nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 states how well it works. No figure exists for how many registrations produce a card, how long the step takes, or what happens to the [39.2% of children aged nought to four registered at the 2024 census](2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos) — the population the link is supposed to serve. The maternity-ward posts reported above are the operational answer being built, and they are in one province.

summary: A bill [would make the identity card the only valid document for banking, telecoms, school enrolment and contracts](2026-04-29-bi-documento-unico-valido-identificacao), and [a law makes it the sole electoral credential from 2027](2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report).
developments:
2026-04-29 — the Council of Ministers [approved a bill making the identity card the only valid document for banking, telecommunications, school enrolment, property registration and contracts](2026-04-29-bi-documento-unico-valido-identificacao), replacing an arrangement in which voter cards, driving licences and passports are accepted substitutes. No parliamentary stage has followed.

Separately, [an official electoral registration law replaces in-person enrolment with automatic enrolment drawn from the civil identity database, with the voter card used for the last time in 2027 and the identity card becoming the sole registration credential thereafter](2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report). No gazette reference is on file and the law reaches the base through a secondary account.

Both make the card load-bearing for services it does not yet reach: [52.4% of the population aged five and over holds one](2025-11-26-quase-metade-dos-angolanos-sem-bilhete-de-identidade). Nothing on the ledger records an authentication service, an interface or a verification volume behind either instrument.

summary: The central bank [completed migration of domestic payments to the international messaging standard on 10 July 2026](2026-07-16-bna-conclui-migracao-iso-20022), across the switch, exchange and settlement participants.
developments:
2026-07-16 — the central bank [announced completion of the migration of domestic payments to the ISO 20022 messaging standard on 10 July 2026, across the switch, the exchange and the real-time settlement participants](2026-07-16-bna-conclui-migracao-iso-20022).

Only the completion is dated. No programme start, scope document or cost is held, and no participant count, message volume or exception rate is published, so the base records that the migration finished and nothing about what it changed.

It is the one act of payments-system governance on this ledger for the window. The instant payment scheme and the regional settlement arrangement reported below both run under this bank, and neither carries a supervisory statement, a scheme rulebook or an oversight report on the base.

summary: The cash-transfer programme [reached more than 1.3 million households and about 6.5 million citizens](2026-07-25-angola-cadastro-social-unico-launch), against 247,000 households at the prior position.
developments:
2026-07-25 — the programme [is reported at more than 1.3 million households and about 6.5 million citizens reached, with a single social register now the centralised targeting database](2026-07-25-angola-cadastro-social-unico-launch), against a starting position of [a US$320m loan building the social registry and government-to-person rails, with more than 247,000 households reached against a 1.6 million family target](2019-06-28 World Bank - Strengthening the National Social Protection System Project (Angola)).

That is the largest measured government-to-person payment operation on this ledger by an order of magnitude. What is not published is the payment instrument: no source states how the transfers reach households, what share is paid into a wallet or an account rather than in cash, or what it costs to deliver.

No data-protection basis or governing instrument was stated for the register at launch, which is reported under registries.

summary: Mandatory electronic invoicing [reached 51,245 enrolled taxpayers and 36,341,801 invoices by August 2026](2026-08-23-more-than-50000-taxpayers-adhere-to-electronic-invoicing-angola), covering large taxpayers and state suppliers.
developments:
2026-08-23 — [51,245 large taxpayers and state suppliers were enrolled and 36,341,801 invoices issued](2026-08-23-more-than-50000-taxpayers-adhere-to-electronic-invoicing-angola), against a mandate [in force from 1 January 2026](2025-12-09-agt-facturacao-electronica-a-partir-de-janeiro-2026) after [an earlier postponement](2025-10-02 Angola - Mandatory e-invoicing implementation postponed) and with no enrolment figure published before this one.

The figures are the tax authority's own and the mandate covers large taxpayers and state suppliers rather than all taxpayers, so this is neither universal coverage nor an independently verified count. The enforcement side is blunt and already live: [a taxpayer not invoicing electronically cannot be paid by the State](2026-02-10-agt-interoperabilidade-certidao-tributaria-orgaos-estado-angolano).

It is the largest transaction volume of any government digital system on this ledger, and it runs on a public key infrastructure that has no governing law, reported under authentication.

summary: The instant payment scheme [is wallet-led, with the largest wallet at 52.2% of transfers and 66.4% of transfers under Kz 10,000](2026-03-05-paypay-ultrapassa-16-milhoes-transferencias-no-kwik).
developments:
2026-03-05 — the monthly operator report [puts the scheme as wallet-led and concentrated: the largest wallet at 52.2% of transfers, more than 12.3m registered accounts, about 24.8m active payment keys, and 66.4% of transfers under Kz 10,000](2026-03-05-paypay-ultrapassa-16-milhoes-transferencias-no-kwik), against [35m transfers and Kz 590bn over 2025 across 22 banking and non-banking institutions](2026-01-29-operacoes-no-kwik-crescimento-acima-dos-100).

The small-value share is the finding: this is retail person-to-person traffic, and the concentration in one wallet is a single point of failure the record does not discuss. The base holds no launch date and no figure dated before 2025, so the growth rate cited by the operator cannot be checked against an independent series.

Nothing on the ledger covers business-to-business or business-to-government payment functionality except through the tax authority's invoicing mandate, reported under revenue collection.

summary: Financial inclusion [stood at 51.7% in the first quarter of 2026 against a 65% target for 2027](2026-07-09-nova-etapa-estrategia-nacional-de-inclusao-financeira), with banking at 32% and digital payments up about 56%.
developments:
2026-07-09 — a state minister's scorecard [puts financial inclusion at 51.7% at the first quarter of 2026 against a 65% target for 2027, banking at 32% or 5.7m people, and mobile and digital payments up about 56% year on year](2026-07-09-nova-etapa-estrategia-nacional-de-inclusao-financeira). The strategy behind the figures launched in December 2025 and no pre-strategy baseline is held, so the target is measurable and the movement toward it is not.

The bancarisation figure has no series behind it either: [a 2023 industry account put roughly half the population unbanked](2023-06-26 Mobile Money in Angola - How Afrimoney is paving the way) on a different base, and the two cannot be read as a trend.

The next phase is stated as letting mobile and digital payment providers extend credit, which would move the same population from payments into lending with no consumer-protection instrument on this ledger behind it.

summary: The kwanza [became the second settlement currency in the regional payment system on 27 July 2026](2026-07-28-sadc-rtgs-kwanza-official), against about US$3.77bn of flows with member states.
developments:
2026-07-28 — the two central-bank governors [formally introduced the kwanza into the regional real-time settlement system, the second settlement currency in its history, against 2025 trade and interbank flows with the other fourteen member states of about US$3.77bn across nine currencies](2026-07-28-sadc-rtgs-kwanza-official), after [integration was announced in May](2026-05-27-kwanza-integra-sistema-de-pagamento-sadc-rtgs). The system had cleared in one currency since 2013.

No volume settled in kwanza has been published since, and no retail cross-border service appears anywhere on this ledger: this is interbank settlement, not remittances or merchant payments. What it changes is which currency regional trade can be invoiced and cleared in, and the test of it will be a settled-value series that does not yet exist.

summary: A presidential decree [created an interministerial commission to de-duplicate and update the adult-citizen database](2026-06-08-pr-cria-comissao-actualizacao-dados-cidadaos-maiores-bdcm), carrying [a US$275m supplementary credit](2026-02-26-credito-suplementar-275-milhoes-usd-mat-bdcm).
developments:
2026-06-08 — [a presidential decree created an interministerial commission to stabilise civil-identification and adult-citizen database interoperability, biometrically de-duplicate, update residence and consolidate the electoral base](2026-06-08-pr-cria-comissao-actualizacao-dados-cidadaos-maiores-bdcm). No technical standard, interface or completion date is on file.

2026-02-26 — the money came first: [US$275,000,000 was opened inside the 2026 budget for the proof-of-life update of the adult-citizen database, more than doubling the territorial administration ministry's allocation](2026-02-26-credito-suplementar-275-milhoes-usd-mat-bdcm), on reporting rather than a held gazetted order.

The register is the base of the electoral roll, which is why the proof-of-life operation reported under the electoral register is contested. A biometric de-duplication of the adult population, financed at this scale and governed by a commission rather than a statute, has no data-protection basis stated anywhere on this ledger.

progress: Advanced, though the youngest cohort is registering worst
summary: Birth registration [reached 63.0% overall but only 39.2% among children aged nought to four](2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos), with [registration posts rehabilitated in two provinces](2026-04-06-projecto-njila-reabilita-postos-de-registo-bie-huambo).
developments:
2025-11-20 — census definitive results [put birth registration at 63.0% overall and 39.2% among children aged nought to four, from 53.5% and 24.8% at the 2014 census](2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos). Both rose, and the gap between them is the finding: the pipeline that feeds the identity card is under-registering the newest cohort fastest.

2026-04-06 — under a US$250m local-governance project, [eleven birth-registration posts were rehabilitated in one province with five operating since August 2025, thirteen more were nearing completion in another, and mass registration campaigns reached several thousand people](2026-04-06-projecto-njila-reabilita-postos-de-registo-bie-huambo), on [a project running across eight provinces and 53 municipalities](2023-01-01-world-bank-ago-2023-projecto-njila-registration-bw10). Only two provinces have published delivery counts.

Nothing on the ledger states a national registration target, a backlog figure or a death-registration rate.

The education ministry made school enrolment independent of documentation: circular 05/2026 of 19 August 2026 orders every school teaching primary and first-cycle secondary education to enrol children holding no birth certificate and no identity card, and to compile by the end of October a survey of undocumented pupils for the justice ministry's registry directorate, whose services are then to travel to the schools and register them ([circular](2026-08-24-angola-med-matricula-escolas-sem-bi)).

summary: A single social register [launched in the capital in July 2026](2026-07-25-angola-cadastro-social-unico-launch) as the centralised targeting database, with no governing instrument stated.
developments:
2026-07-25 — [a single national social registry launched to map vulnerable households and act as the centralised database directing social supports](2026-07-25-angola-cadastro-social-unico-launch), replacing a position in which social-transfer targeting rested on one programme's own registry.

No enrolment target, data-protection basis, interoperability plan or governing instrument was stated at launch. That is the whole of the record: a database of the country's poorest households, built to direct payments to them, with nothing published about who may read it, how long it holds what it holds, or which other system it connects to.

The transfer programme it now targets is reported under government-to-person payments, and reached about 6.5 million citizens.

summary: A proof-of-life operation [runs 254 of a planned 634 counters against a universe of 16,707,455 citizens](2026-08-19-novojornal-angola-oposicao-registo-eleitoral-obstaculos), and four opposition parties demand an independent audit.
developments:
2026-06-15 — [the proof-of-life operation to update the electoral register opened](2026-06-15-arranca-prova-de-vida-para-actualizacao-do-registo-eleitoral). By August, [254 of a planned 634 counters were live across all 21 provinces and the diaspora, with 10,747 field workers against a target universe of 16,707,455 citizens, and over 730,000 updated nationally on the opposition's count](2026-08-19-novojornal-angola-oposicao-registo-eleitoral-obstaculos).

The count is the problem. The electoral administration has published no enrolment figure since the operation opened, so the only national number the base holds comes from a political declaration by four parties that are contesting the operation. They allege administrative discretion, uneven deployment of registration brigades and recurring biometric-system failures, and say the administration refuses to release statistics disaggregated by province, municipality and commune, which blocks any audit of the register's real flow; the electoral commission had earlier refused accreditation to a civic monitor. None of it has been adjudicated and no official series exists to test it against.

At provincial level, [one government reports over 40,000 residents updated and is pressing mining-sector workers to register through one-stop service desks](2026-08-20-angop-lunda-norte-governor-electoral-data-update). Ahead of all of it, [a law replaces in-person registration with automatic enrolment from the civil identity database, with the voter card used for the last time in 2027](2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report).

summary: A digital platform [linking the cadastre, the tax authority and the property registry targets 40,000 properties legalised by end-2026](2026-04-17-plataforma-digital-legalizacao-de-40-mil-imoveis), with no progress published since.
developments:
2026-04-17 — [a digital platform linking the cadastre, the tax authority and the property registry was set a target of 40,000 properties legalised by the end of 2026, aimed at cutting duplication and enabling mortgage access](2026-04-17-plataforma-digital-legalizacao-de-40-mil-imoveis).

No progress figure against that target has been published in the four months since, and no source states whether the platform is in service, which agency operates it or how the three registries it links exchange data. A target with no reporting against it is the same shape of evidence as the digital transition agenda's project count: a number the government publishes about its own intentions.

It is the only land or property system on this ledger.

summary: The vaccination registry [is in use across all national campaigns](2026-02-14-angola-inovacao-digital-no-sistema-de-saude-rediv-dhis2), with interoperability to the national health information system still under development, and a [regional surveillance operation closed](2025-11-30-worldbank-icr-redisse-iv-health-surveillance) in November 2025.
developments:
2026-02-14 — [the vaccination registry is described as in use across all national vaccination campaigns, with interoperability to the national health information system under development](2026-02-14-angola-inovacao-digital-no-sistema-de-saude-rediv-dhis2). It was already in use for real-time individual vaccination registration at the start of the window, so the position is unchanged.

A secretary of state's conference remarks are the only source. No coverage figure, record count, facility count or evaluation is published, and no other health information system appears anywhere on this ledger — no electronic medical record, no health facility registry and no laboratory or supply-chain system.

The one prospective addition is a vendor memorandum on digital health reported under geopolitics, against which no delivery has been reported.

2025-11-30 - the World Bank's implementation completion report [closed REDISSE Phase IV, a US$280m five-country regional disease-surveillance operation carrying a health information and ICT subcomponent at 14% of the sector share and naming DHIS2, IDSR and EWARS among its systems](2025-11-30-worldbank-icr-redisse-iv-health-surveillance). The held capture is an excerpt: it states no country-specific system, coverage or outcome, so what the operation left behind here is not on the record.

summary: A national education database initiative [launched in August 2026 under a five-year, thirty-country data challenge](2026-08-19-adea-angola-education-skills-data-challenge), alongside [a national education and research network](2026-05-14-angola-unveils-angoren-network).
developments:
2026-08-19 — [a structured multi-year effort with the education ministry, a continental education association and an in-country technical partner launched to strengthen the national education database and the capacity to turn statistics into policy, under a five-year, thirty-country data challenge](2026-08-19-adea-angola-education-skills-data-challenge), [presented at a Luanda event in early August](2026-08-07-angola-med-mwango-brain-base-nacional-dados). No data-quality baseline, scope, budget or completion date is published, and no contract or programme document is held.

2026-05-14 — separately, [a national education and research network was presented alongside an executive roadmap for higher-education digital transformation](2026-05-14-angola-unveils-angoren-network), with no connected institutions, capacity, funding or operating date stated.

Both are announcements of intent. Nothing on the ledger records an enrolment system, a school census platform or a teacher registry in operation.

summary: Tax-compliance certificates [are automated inside the tax authority, with extension to banks and other state bodies under way](2026-02-10-agt-interoperabilidade-certidao-tributaria-orgaos-estado-angolano).
developments:
2026-02-10 — [customs clearance was automated for compliant taxpayers inside the tax authority, with extension of the compliance certificate to banks and other state bodies under way](2026-02-10-agt-interoperabilidade-certidao-tributaria-orgaos-estado-angolano). No baseline was published before it.

The order of arrival is worth recording: the enforcement side is already live — a taxpayer not invoicing electronically cannot be paid by the State — while the interoperability the enforcement rests on is still being built. [The authority is separately phasing out paper documents](2026-05-23-agt-eliminacao-gradual-documentos-em-papel).

This is the most operationally advanced sectoral system on the ledger, measured by the volumes reported under revenue collection, and it is also the one running furthest ahead of the legal instruments that would govern it.

summary: A logistics single window [is to absorb the port, foreign-trade and customs platforms into one](2026-07-28-angola-arccla-logistics-single-window-integration), with phase one expected between late 2026 and mid-2027.
developments:
2026-07-28 — [an integrated logistics single window was announced to absorb three separate agency platforms into one, framed explicitly as a formalisation and tax-base instrument rather than as trade facilitation, with phase one expected between the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027](2026-07-28-angola-arccla-logistics-single-window-integration).

A board communique is the only source. No instrument, budget or vendor is named, and no baseline is published for what the three existing platforms handle. The framing is the notable part: a customs and logistics integration justified by revenue rather than by clearance times, which is consistent with the tax authority's other work reported above.

summary: No inventory of online services exists — [the transition agenda counts projects, not services](2026-03-05-governo-aposta-reorganizacao-administracao-publica-governo-digital-2027) — while [an at-home identity-card service](2026-07-28-angop-minjus-lanca-servico-bi-ao-domicilio) and [a public-finance programme](2026-08-17-correiokianda-angola-public-finance-digital-programme) launched.
developments:
What is missing first: [no service catalogue is published and the transition agenda counts projects rather than services](2026-03-05-governo-aposta-reorganizacao-administracao-publica-governo-digital-2027), so the count of public services available online is not knowable from the record.

2026-07-28 — [an at-home identity-card service launched in one province at Kz 250,000 for at-home processing and Kz 10,000 for delivery alone, on a 48-hour issuance target, with requests through a web portal and a messaging number](2026-07-28-angop-minjus-lanca-servico-bi-ao-domicilio). [The ministry called the fee a product of exclusivity](2026-07-28-angola-home-delivery-id-card-fee), and no ministry publication naming the portal is on file.

2026-08-17 — [a programme to modernise finance ministry services and restructure state bodies was authorised by presidential order as a direct award](2026-08-17-correiokianda-angola-public-finance-digital-programme). Its value is not established: [the earlier of the two accounts, whose reporter says he saw the order, gives three different figures in one article](2026-08-12-valoreconomico-angola-financas-publicas-transformacao-digital), and the later reproduces its lead almost word for word.

The health ministry's recruitment competition shows what online registration costs when it goes wrong: of more than 420,000 who registered in July 2026, more than 170,000 were excluded for defective registration, leaving more than 262,000 to sit tests for 6,030 posts on 21-25 September, sat nationwide and marked online ([competition](2026-08-25-angola-minsa-concurso-publico-262-mil-candidatos)).

summary: A provincial water utility [begins installing 25,000-26,000 prepaid smart meters from 7 September 2026](2026-08-26-angola-benguela-agua-pre-pago-contadores) on a stated USD 23 million budget.
developments: Benguela's provincial water utility begins installing prepaid smart meters on 7 September 2026, targeting 25,000 to 26,000 by March 2027 on a stated USD 23 million budget drawn from a USD 191.3 million rehabilitation project across five municipalities ([meters](2026-08-26-angola-benguela-agua-pre-pago-contadores)). It follows a USD 15 million registration exercise that produced a 70,000-client database, replacing estimate-based billing against arrears stated above 10 billion kwanzas ([meters](2026-08-26-angola-benguela-agua-pre-pago-contadores)).

summary: One provincial government [approved an integrated document and archive management system in December 2025](2025-12-18-cubango-transicao-administracao-analogica-para-digital-sigda), budgeting around weak internet and power.
developments:
2025-12-18 — [a provincial government approved integrated document and archive management with a citizen application for proposals and public-tender tracking, implementation from January 2026, budgeting explicitly around weak internet and power](2025-12-18-cubango-transicao-administracao-analogica-para-digital-sigda).

The stated six-month operationalisation target passed with nothing on file either way. It is the only sub-national digitalisation instrument on this ledger for any of the country's provinces, and no source records what the other twenty do with their records.

The design assumption is the useful part: a system specified for intermittent connectivity and power is the right shape for a country where mains electricity reaches few rural households, reported under energy.

summary: The president [authorised US$6 million and a public tender for an artificial-intelligence platform for the public administration](2026-09-01-ago-executivo-desembolsa-usd-6-milhoes-para-plataforma-de-inteli), the base's first record of money committed to one.
developments:
A presidential order of 27 August 2026 authorised expenditure of six million United States dollars for the acquisition and implementation of an artificial-intelligence platform for the public administration, and opened a public tender procedure for it ([order](2026-09-01-ago-executivo-desembolsa-usd-6-milhoes-para-plataforma-de-inteli)).

The order authorises money and a procurement. What the platform is to do, which bodies would use it, on what data, and under what governance are not stated in the announcement, and no strategy or policy instrument on artificial intelligence in government is held to read it against.

summary: The tax authority's [machine-learning risk-analysis system began testing in 2024 with first taxpayer notices due from June 2026](2026-02-11-inteligencia-artificial-coloca-incumpridores-sob-analise-reforcada-da-agt), built in-house.
developments:
2026-02-11 — [the tax authority reported machine-learning testing begun in 2024 and first taxpayer notices due from June 2026, on a system it states it builds and feeds in-house](2026-02-11-inteligencia-artificial-coloca-incumpridores-sob-analise-reforcada-da-agt). No baseline was published before it and the system is not in service.

No model, supplier or accuracy figure is published, and no taxpayer-facing safeguard is stated beyond a right to be heard — against a draft artificial-intelligence law that would give a right to explanation and to refuse decisions made by artificial intelligence, and which has not been tabled.

It is the only use of artificial intelligence inside a government sectoral system on this ledger. No health, education, justice or social-protection system reports any.

progress: Advanced, one commercial assistant, with no installed compute behind it
summary: An operator [launched a web version of its AI assistant in July 2026](2026-07-22-africell-afrigpt-web), and [no held source states any installed accelerator capacity or named AI facility](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia).
developments:
2026-07-22 — [a subscription web assistant pitched at student research launched at a trade fair, replacing a text-message version, offered by an operator reporting seven million clients across five provinces](2026-07-22-africell-afrigpt-web). The source confirms a prior version but does not date it, and no usage figure and no model provenance is published — so what is built locally, if anything, is not established.

Underneath it there is no compute. [No held source states an installed accelerator capacity, an AI cloud or a named AI facility](2026-06-30-unesco-ram-angola-28000km-fibra-prontidao-ia), and the readiness assessment's own infrastructure case rests on fibre, one satellite and data centres rather than on anything AI-specific.

The government data centre reported under storage is the only national compute estate on the ledger, and nothing states that any of it is allocated to this.

summary: No supervisory authority exists: [the draft law provides for a competent authority and leaves its designation, powers and seat to a future regulation](2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial).
developments:
[The draft artificial-intelligence law provides for a competent authority at article 61 and leaves its designation, powers and seat to a future regulation](2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial). No authority exists, and the bill has not been tabled.

[The same review notes that the draft repeals no existing legislation and that its financial assessment is not costed](2025-12-29 Review of Angola's Proposed Law on Artificial Intelligence), so nothing states who would fund or staff the body it provides for.

Control of abuse currently runs through instruments written for other purposes: the false-information law reported under public debate reaches platforms and application providers, and the data-protection authority reported under data protection has the only enforcement record on this ledger. Neither addresses automated decision-making, and no case involving an AI system has been recorded by either.

summary: A science and technology park [was inaugurated in June 2026 under a US$100m development-bank project](2026-06-29-angola-launches-luanda-technology-park), and [a public-finance innovation lab launched](2026-03-30-angola-launches-i-lab-public-finance-techafricanews).
developments:
2026-06-29 — [a science and technology park was inaugurated under a US$100m development-bank science and technology project, intended to link academia, research, companies and young entrepreneurs](2026-06-29-angola-launches-luanda-technology-park). No tenant, occupancy, disbursement or operating budget is published.

2026-03-30 — [a finance-ministry innovation lab launched, its first proof of concept qualified digital signatures in an internally built document system](2026-03-30-angola-launches-i-lab-public-finance-techafricanews), with no budget, headcount or project pipeline published.

Against them, [an incubation programme agreed in March 2025 offering institutional and technical support, physical space, training and investor introductions](2025-03-18-angolan-agencies-join-forces-to-strengthen-nascent-startup-sector) has published no cohort, intake number, graduate or funding outcome in seventeen months. Two new buildings and no reported occupants is the shape of the evidence.

progress: Mixed, a startups law passed while the innovation ranking fell to 138th of 139
summary: A startups law [passed unanimously with a revenue-ceiling definition](2026-03-23-angola-passes-landmark-start-up-law), while [the innovation ranking fell to 138th of 139 economies](2025-01-01 WIPO Global Innovation Index 2025 - Angola profile).
developments:
2026-03-23 — [a startups law passed unanimously, defining a startup at an annual revenue ceiling of about US$3.5m with no minimum threshold, so pre-revenue ventures qualify](2026-03-23-angola-passes-landmark-start-up-law), after [passage in generality four days earlier](2026-03-19-proposta-de-lei-das-startups-aprovada-na-generalidade). Promulgation and gazette number are not held.

The population it addresses has not moved. [Fewer than 2% of identified startups have secured venture funding, with angel and seed structures largely absent](2026-03-23-angola-passes-landmark-start-up-law), against about 125 startups and no exit event at the last assessment; no newer count has been published, including by the ministry that sponsored the law. The one visible venture is [the country's only entrant in a fifteen-startup accelerator cohort drawn from about 2,600 applications, raising US$4.6m across named investors on AI-powered credit scoring for motorcycle-taxi work](2026-04-21 Meet the 15 Startups Joining the Google for Startups Accelerator Africa Class 10).

[The innovation ranking fell to 138th of 139 economies, worse on outputs than inputs and with no cluster in the world's top innovation clusters](2025-01-01 WIPO Global Innovation Index 2025 - Angola profile), on a six-year trend running 132nd, 127th, 132nd, 133rd and now 138th.

summary: A presidential order authorised the training of local agents, framed as the step that follows investment in digital infrastructure ([order](2026-08-27-ago-formacao-agentes-locais-pada)).
developments: A presidential order authorised the training of local agents, framed as the step that follows investment in digital infrastructure ([order](2026-08-27-ago-formacao-agentes-locais-pada)). No participant target or curriculum is stated.

summary: No national digital-literacy programme exists — [the base carries it only as clauses inside other instruments](2024-10-11-worldbank-loan-agreement-9693-ao-angola-digital-acceleration) — and the loan's grants component still has no allocation.
developments:
[The base carries digital literacy only as clauses inside other instruments, with no national programme, budget line, target or trained-population figure](2024-10-11-worldbank-loan-agreement-9693-ao-angola-digital-acceleration). A ministry or education programme document would settle it and none is held.

The one named vehicle is a loan component: [grants to non-governmental and community groups for community digital spaces and digital literacy, still with no allocation, grantee, disbursement or beneficiary count](2024-10-11-worldbank-loan-agreement-9693-ao-angola-digital-acceleration) two years after it was named. [The same loan carries a target of 100,000 people trained through digital literacy programmes by March 2030](2026-07-31-pada-projecto-aceleracao-digital-abrange-10-milhoes-de-pessoas), and every outcome indicator under it reads zero, reported under development-partner financing.

The school laboratory programme reported under training is real and is a different thing: hardware in schools, not a literacy programme for the population.

summary: School computer laboratories [total more than 2,000 computers across 88 schools on the minister's own count](2026-08-21-angop-ipas-laboratorio-ngola-digital), the latest serving 3,051 students.
developments:
2026-08-21 — [a 25-computer laboratory was inaugurated at a polytechnic serving 3,051 students, bringing the programme to more than 2,000 computers installed across 88 schools nationwide on the telecommunications minister's own count](2026-08-21-angop-ipas-laboratorio-ngola-digital).

The totals are the minister's and no programme budget, connectivity provision or maintenance arrangement is published. Nothing states what is taught on the machines, whether any of the 88 schools has a connection, or who repairs them.

It is the only school-level intervention on this ledger, and it is hardware. No curriculum instrument, teacher-training programme or examination in a digital subject appears anywhere for the country.

summary: A satellite-technology training programme [gave more than 5,600 university students free access and trained a Luanda cohort of more than 100](2026-06-03-university-of-namibe-students-free-internet-angosat-2).
developments:
